newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Ipoh sees 25 pct rise in '96 div.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Ipoh sees 25 pct rise in '96 div.

text.p: Property developer and investor Ipoh Ltd said on Wednesday it expected calendar 1996 net profit to fall to A$8.7 million but the total dividend to rise by 25 percent.

The Malaysian-controlled company, which owns the Queen Victoria Building retail centre in central Sydney, achieved 1995 net profit of A$15.3 million but this included a one-off gain from the 55 percent sale of Sydney's historic Capitol Theatre.
In documents prepared for a press briefing, Ipoh said the 1996 profit forecast included a first-time tax payment.
Annual dividend would rise to 15 cents from 12 cents.
Calendar 1997 net profit was estimated to be A$11.6 million.
The company said gross rent from the Queen Victoria Building would be A$29.5 million this year and A$32.8 million in 1997 compared with A$28.1 million in 1995.
Earnings before interest and tax were estimated to be A$22.8 million this calendar year and A$25.4 million in 1997 compared with A$20.2 million in 1995.
The company's largest shareholder is IGB Corp Bhd with a 39 percent stake. Chairman Dato Yap Lim Sen is the next largest investor with a 12 percent holding.
